Arman vs State Of U.P.Through Prin. Sec.Home ... on 20
February, 2023

Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh
Bench: Sanjay Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 5328 of 2022
Applicant :- Arman

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.Through Prin. Sec.Home Gov.Of U.P. And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Jawahir Yadav,Anoop Kumar Sharma,Sanjay Kumar Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Brij Bhushan Pandey Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and Mr. K.M. Tripathi, learned Advocate holding brief of Mr. B.B.Pandey, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the first informant.

By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant, who is involved in Case Crime No. 224 of 2021, under sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Nijamabad, District Azamgarh, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

As per prosecution case, in brief, the informant who is grand-father of the victim has lodged an FIR on 12.11.2021 against the applicant with the allegation inter-alia that on 12.11.2021 at about 04:30 pm when his grand-daughter had gone to market to purchase some goods, she was enticed away by the present applicant.
Arman vs State Of U.P.Through Prin. Sec.Home ... on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13455563/
1 The main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that as per ossification test report, victim is major, aged about 18 years.

It is next argued that the victim was consenting party with the applicant and she herself gone to Lucknow with the applicant, therefore, applicant who is languishing in jail since 09.12.2021 is entitled for bail.

Per-contra, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the victim is minor girl and as per her High School Certificate, her date of birth is 01.01.2007, therefore, on the date of incident, she was aged about 14 years 10 months and 11 days.

The victim in her statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has made allegation of rape against the applicant and she has also stated that the applicant,
extending threat, dragged her into his car and took her to Lucknow where she was in the captivity of the applicant and applicant also made physical relation with her.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that the victim is minor and she has also supported the prosecution case making allegation of rape against the applicant.
At this stage, I do not find any material on record to presume that the victim was consenting party with the applicant and to disbelieve the statement of the victim.
Prima-facie, no case for bail is made out.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the submissions advanced on behalf of parties, gravity of offence, role assigned to applicant and severity of punishment, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected at this stage.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.

However considering the detention period of the applicant since 09.12.2021, it is expected that the trial court shall make an endeavour to conclude the trial, expeditiously, without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.

Order Date :- 20.2.2023 Saurabh  Arman vs State Of U.P.Through Prin. Sec.Home ... on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13455563/
